key_insight: PanoWorld turns panoramic rotation into a geometric advantage: by leveraging rotation-equivariant omnidirectional representations, it can model camera motion and long-range memory more effectively in 360° environments. This simplifies panoramic trajectory modeling while preserving spatial consistency over time.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the long-range memory challenge in panoramic world models, where maintaining coherent scene understanding across extended camera movements is difficult, especially in omnidirectional 360° settings.
method: Uses rotation-equivariant panoramic representations so rotational changes are treated as implicit geometric transformations.
Introduces Dense Panoramic Ray-Conditioning (DPRC) to model current action and scene dynamics with fixed headings.
Adds geometry-aware memory mechanisms to retain long-range information and support consistent panoramic world generation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, PanoWorld offers a more structured way to build world models for 360° data, improving memory retention and trajectory consistency. This can benefit robotics, VR/AR, autonomous navigation, and any application that relies on panoramic scene understanding.
